Defensible claim: OECD and ISO methods can provide an assay framework when the selected test, organism, endpoint, and laboratory conditions match.
Scope limit: A test method is not evidence that a particular machine or material is conformant.
Required evidence before stronger claim: Laboratory protocol, accredited or documented lab practice, raw data, QA/QC record, and interpretation report.

Defensible claim: An ISO 14040-style lifecycle methodology can structure a carbon claim.
Scope limit: A methodology reference is not a measured negative-emissions result.
Required evidence before stronger claim: Functional unit, baseline, inventory data, allocation choices, uncertainty analysis, critical review, and update frequency.

Defensible claim: Offline-first industrial design is an established engineering pattern.
Scope limit: Existence of the pattern does not establish safety or fitness of a particular mechanism.
Required evidence before stronger claim: Equipment-specific integration tests, hazard analysis, safety interlocks, dry-run and field commissioning evidence, rollback/bypass procedures.

Defensible claim: Separating private governance context from machine credentials is sound privacy and access-control architecture.
Scope limit: A DID alone is not consent, identity proof, authority, or a control credential.
Required evidence before stronger claim: Purpose specification, key-management policy, revocation process, access policy, audit controls, and consent basis where applicable.

Defensible claim: Total-function policy semantics and database constraints can encode reviewable governance rules.
Scope limit: A formal artifact only proves properties of the model under its stated assumptions.
Required evidence before stronger claim: Parser/validator, executable constraint tests, migration tests, adversarial inputs, and human review.
